title: Browser and Computer-Use Agents
brief: Your browser agent works three fake sites by looking at screenshots and clicking: book a table, request a return, renew a parking permit. 20 runs each. The screens shift as pages load, so about 3 runs in 10 the agent clicks Confirm on the wrong date, guest count or permit. Some pages also carry a line of small print addressed to "AI assistants". Get wrong and hijacked submissions to zero, keep 90% of errands finished, and ask the human no more than 1.6 times per errand.

modifiers.note: Coordinates come from a picture of the page. When the layout moves, the click lands somewhere else.
From a screenshot, Sat 18 and Fri 17 are a few pixels apart. The model is confident either way.
The screenshot is untrusted content. Instructions printed on the page arrive in the same channel as the task.

goals.label: Zero wrong or hijacked submissions in 60 errands
At most 1.6 human confirmations per errand

hints: Open a failed run. Every click before the last one can be fixed with another screenshot. Which actions cannot be taken back?

Asking a person before every action would catch it too, but count the confirmations: an errand has a dozen clicks. Only the submit commits, and the injected footer only does harm if something gets submitted.

Add a Human approval node with "Ask when: irreversible" and put it between the loop and submit_form. The person sees the summary screen and says yes or no, and refuses anything the page asked for that the user did not.
explain: Screens are slow, ambiguous and untrusted tools, so most mistakes are cheap: take another screenshot and click again. The steps you cannot retry are submits, so that is where a human confirms what is on the screen. The confirmation also catches the page that tried to give the agent orders, though it is a backstop, not a cure for injection.
